conventions.convention: Heegaard splittings use two orientable handlebodies of equal genus and an orientation-reversing boundary diffeomorphism.
In orientation-compatible annular product coordinates, the positive twist is (θ,t) ↦ (θ+2πρ(t),t), with ρ zero near the lower endpoint and one near the upper endpoint.
An integer framing n fills along nμ+λ, where λ is the preferred longitude in the individual component's knot exterior. The empty diagram presents the standard oriented S³. Full AC is assumed.
Kirby equivalence is generated by orientation-preserving ambient isotopy, band slides carrying the full normal framing, and insertion or deletion of split ±1-framed unknots.
The zero-meridian pair uses the positively oriented small meridian of its companion knot, with disk framing zero; the companion framing and its linking with the old link are unrestricted.
The worked lens-space examples use L(p,q)=E_U(p/q), with p>0; in particular positive p-framed unknot surgery is L(p,1).

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let D₀ and D₁ be finite integral framed-link surgery diagrams in the standard oriented 3-sphere, with surgery results M₀ and M₁. Then M₀ and M₁ are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic if and only if D₀ and D₁ are related by a finite sequence of ambient isotopies, framed handle slides, and additions or deletions of split ±1-framed unknots.

Under AC, a finite oriented link in the standard oriented S³, with chosen disjoint tubular neighbourhoods, peripheral data and component integers nᵢ, defines simultaneous surgery by filling each component along nᵢμᵢ+λᵢ. The empty link gives S³; diagrams are considered up to orientation-preserving ambient isotopy carrying the component framings.

Assume AC. For a finite integral framed link L in standard oriented S³, any integer-framed knot K in its complement together with its positively oriented small disk-zero-framed meridian U can be inserted or deleted by a finite sequence of orientation-preserving ambient isotopies, fully framed slides and split ±1-framed unknot moves, without restrictions on K's knot type or linking with L.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. If two integral framed-link surgery diagrams are related by one ambient isotopy, handle slide, or split ±1-unknot stabilization or destabilization as defined for this page, then their oriented surgery results are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic. The same holds for any finite sequence of these moves.

Assume AC. Every nonempty closed connected oriented smooth 3-manifold is orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic to simultaneous integral surgery on a finite oriented link in S³, with meridian slopes nᵢμᵢ+λᵢ. The empty link is allowed and presents S³.

published_dependencies.used_for: Ambient, surface and handlebody orientation conventions.
Embedded circles, links and handlebody constructions.
The full-choice hypotheses and their implication of countable choice.
The collar, tubular, surgery-trace and handle-slide interfaces.
A finite smooth triangulation in the Heegaard existence proof.
The framed disk-factor replacement in the Dehn-twist surgery lemma.
Finite oriented links, orientation-preserving ambient isotopy and preservation of component count.
Actual smooth oriented framed-link surgery existence from base S³ in the Lickorish–Wallace proof.
Identification of link band slides with fully framed four-dimensional two-handle slides.
The four-dimensional trace and its extending orientation.
A slide comparison relative to the incoming face, with k=2 and ambient dimension four.
Identification of the outgoing trace boundary with surgery, identity on the unchanged exterior; the owned proof separately checks orientation.
The O1/O2/O3 comparison of the given endpoint presentations in the closed, undecorated fixed-base S³ case.

concerns.concern: Operation 2 specifies a framed parallel Kⱼ⁺ and says to orient the result by the band-sum orientation, but does not explicitly permit either orientation of that parallel while retaining the orientation of Kⱼ. The zero-meridian proof explicitly uses signed parallels in steps 1.1, 2.2 and 5.1. Clarifying this signed-slide convention would remove an ambiguity in the defined move set.

The source locator says “Lemma 2.2 and proof ... printed pp. 33–34”. In the linked second revised edition, Lemma 2.2 starts on printed p. 34 and its proof concludes on p. 35, PDF pages 46–47. The annular construction and meridian shear agree with the cited argument. Source: [Saveliev, Lectures on the Topology of 3-Manifolds](https://poisson.phc.dm.unipi.it/~camponovo/libri/3mani.pdf).

seams_checked.note: The chosen exterior, positive meridian and unique degree-one null-homologous longitude match the opened suppliers. Full AC in the consuming items supplies their countable-choice hypothesis.
Integer surgery consistently uses nμ+λ. The examples explicitly adopt the supplier's L(p,q)=E_U(p/q) orientation convention, including p=1.

The TQFT theorem uses Kirby classification for closed oriented surgery outputs under full AC. Its bordism construction is separately supplied, rather than inferred from this closed-manifold classification.
The half-twist lifting lemma cites exactly the positive annular formula for product orientation dθ∧dt and checks its relative sign through an explicit branched-annulus model.
